properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, partly measured): "slash commands don't exist in VS Code chat" is OVERTURNED by VS Code's own documentation. Prompt files (.github/prompts) and Agent Skills (.github/skills, .claude/skills, .agents/skills) are both "/" commands, and skills are chosen by their description. reflow2's part is that init writes its discovery shims only as Claude Code commands in .claude/commands, and writes nothing VS Code reads for skills
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-02, triage agent B. Item L7 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02: "Skills are not native in a thin-installed project, and slash commands don't exist in VS Code chat."

① SPLIT. OBSERVED: no reflow2 skill appears natively in VS Code chat. CONCLUDED: VS Code chat has no slash commands.

② PRECEDENT: req:kit-reaches-the-agent (accepted) and dec:skills-served are the thin-install choice. The planned fix is in req:init-installs-the-terminal-route-for-vs-code-and-update-keeps-it-current (skill stubs in .github/skills) and dec:idea-the-call-door-becomes-a-supported-harness-for-an-agent-that-cannot-use-mcp (idea 7, settled). ALREADY RECORDED as a plan; the conclusion was not checked.

⑤ MEASURED.
(a) VS Code docs, fetched 2026-10-02, code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/:
- prompt-files: "In the Chat view, type `/` followed by the prompt name"; workspace prompts live in ".github/prompts".
- agent-skills: project skills are read from ".github/skills/, .claude/skills/, .agents/skills/". "Copilot reads the skill's name and description from the YAML frontmatter" to pick one. "Skills are available as slash commands in chat, alongside prompt files". `disable-model-invocation: true` makes a skill slash-only.
So the reporter's conclusion is wrong as a statement about VS Code. NOT measured on the work machine: an organisation policy could switch skills or prompt files off there. That is NOT ESTABLISHED.
(b) Code, origin/main 66620f7:
- reflow2_init.py TREES installs KIT/commands into .claude/commands (4-line shims such as gaps.md, "Use the detect-and-ask skill…") and KIT/plugins into .opencode/plugins.
- The `vscode` harness entry writes only .vscode/mcp.json.
- is_skill_path knows .claude/skills and .grok/skills only as directories to PRUNE.
- So a thin-installed project holds nothing VS Code reads as a skill or a prompt.
- The commands also say "use the X skill" without saying how to fetch it, which through the door means `--call get_skill`.

⑥ CLASS: the same as req:kit-reaches-the-agent's own finding, "reach what reads, not what exists". The shims were placed for one harness's directory. VS Code also reads .claude/skills, so a shim written as a SKILL there, rather than as a command, would reach Claude Code and VS Code alike. Untested here.

Verdict: limitation CONFIRMED (no native skills). The report's slash-command conclusion is OVERTURNED by the documentation, and still to be confirmed on the work machine.
